// WorkerPool fans out jobs over a fixed set of workers and collects their
// results in order. It exists so the caller does not have to think about
// goroutine lifetimes at all.
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Job is one unit of work; Result is what comes back for it.
type Job struct {
	ID    int
	Bytes int
}

type Result struct {
	Job  Job
	Took time.Duration
}

/* Run processes jobs over n workers and returns when every job is done.
   The results slice is indexed by job ID, so the order never depends on
   which worker happened to finish first. */
func Run(jobs []Job, n int) []Result {
	results := make([]Result, len(jobs))
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	work := make(chan Job)

	wg.Add(n)
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		go func() {
			defer wg.Done()
			for j := range work {
				start := time.Now()
				time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
				results[j.ID] = Result{Job: j, Took: time.Since(start)}
			}
		}()
	}
	for _, j := range jobs {
		work <- j
	}
	close(work)
	wg.Wait()
	return results
}

func main() {
	jobs := make([]Job, 8)
	for i := range jobs {
		jobs[i] = Job{ID: i, Bytes: 1024}
	}
	for _, r := range Run(jobs, 4) {
		fmt.Printf("job %d took %v\n", r.Job.ID, r.Took)
	}
}
